key_insight: Public AI leaderboards are not static rankings but incomplete time series, and Bayesian reconstruction can reveal that very different evaluation histories are compatible with the same terminal score.
engineering_relevance: For AI evaluation pipelines, this means model claims should be audited against archival history, missingness, and benchmark drift rather than trusted from a single leaderboard snapshot.
method: Reconstruct public evaluation histories from repeated archives of LiveBench and Open LLM Leaderboard v2.
Use Bayesian terminal-tail modeling to infer pre-terminal trajectories and timing-to-ceiling bounds.
Apply audit gates across synthetic recovery, prediction, transfer, and calibration tests to verify or reject frontier claims.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that one terminal-only example over 1,000+ systems is consistent with two different histories, yielding 23.03 or 75.13 time-to-ceiling estimates under the same model.
watch_item: Results depend on archive completeness and reporting conventions, so missing updates or benchmark revisions can still bias reconstructed histories.
paper_title: Bayesian Inference and Decision Audits for Public Archives of Frontier AI Evaluations
